traits.fan_split_depth.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 216): the blade split along its central fold to the middle or nearly to the costa, then along the other folds into single-fold segments; how deep those splits go is not given, so the segments are read as free over a half to four fifths of their length.

traits.segment_posture.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 216): the segments drooping, linear.

traits.segment_filaments.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 216): segments sometimes filiferous, interfold filaments sometimes present; Sargent (1922, p. 101) has the segments often separating into threads at their margins. Read as a few threads.

traits.petiole_armature.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 216): the petiole unarmed, its margins sharp.

traits.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under the genus (Palmae III 1): dwarf or stout unarmed palms with bisexual flowers.

traits.leaf_division.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.

traits.clonal.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: its stems are solitary; its fan leaves are shortly costapalmate, the rib running only a little into the blade.

generator.params.costa.why: The rib the fan's segments rise from, as a share of the frond: a fifth for a strongly costapalmate fan, a tenth for a shortly costapalmate one (the built-in cabbage and California fan palms, 0.18 and 0.12).
